sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a Rochester, Minnesota house?
sections.html:
Olmsted County bills and collects the property tax on Rochester homes, and the county assessor sets the value the bill is built on. One statement covers the county, the city, the school district and any other local taxing district that applies to your parcel.

The office that takes your payment is Olmsted County Property Records and Licensing, at the Government Center, 151 4th Street SE, Rochester, MN 55904. Mail goes to PO Box 6681, Rochester, MN 55903-6681. Call 507-328-7636 about statements, 507-328-7635 about delinquent years, and 507-328-7670 for the assessor.

The assessor values roughly 76,000 parcels in the county as of January 2 each year. State law requires the estimate to track market value, and your value notice arrives in mid-March together with the tax statement. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate puts Rochester at 124,292 residents, third in Minnesota. See the county's property assessments page for the valuation side.

sections.h2: When are Rochester property taxes due, and what does a late payment cost?
sections.html:
Real and personal property tax in Rochester is paid in two halves, due May 15 and October 15. For 2026 the county lists May 15 and October 15 for real and personal property, with agricultural second-half taxes and both manufactured home installments listed separately.

The October 15, 2026 installment has already passed. If it is still open on your parcel, Minnesota Statutes section 279.01 adds a 2 percent penalty on homestead property or 4 percent on nonhomestead property on the due date. A second round of the same size lands on the first day of the next month. After that, 1 percent more accrues each month through December, up to 8 percent for homestead and 12 percent for nonhomestead.

Two statute details help when a payment is close to the line. A bill of $100 or less is due in full on May 15. And if a mailed payment carries a postmark within one business day after the due date, the treasurer must abate the penalty once for that owner. If you mail near a deadline, ask a postal clerk for a hand-applied postmark.

Olmsted County property tax calendar for Rochester owners (source: Olmsted County Property Records and Licensing)

Agricultural second-half tax and the second half for manufactured homes are due November 16, 2026, and the first manufactured home installment was due August 31, 2026.

sections.h2: How do I pay my Olmsted County tax bill from Rochester?
sections.html:
You can pay online, by phone, by mail, by bank bill pay, through automatic withdrawal, or in person. Every method needs the parcel ID from your statement, which looks like RP 74.05.05.000000 for real property.

  • Online: credit card or e-check through the county's property information site. The fee is 3.28 percent for a card and $3.16 for an e-check, and only current-year tax can be paid this way, up to $300,000. A bank can take seven to 10 business days to clear it, and the payment is complete only when the confirmation email arrives.
  • Phone: call 1-800-272-9829 and give jurisdiction number 3336. Current and delinquent tax can both be paid by card or e-check at the same fees.
  • Mail: a check or money order payable to Olmsted County with the stub from your statement. Allow five to seven business days for delivery.
  • In person: the Government Center takes cash, checks, money orders and cards, with a 2.15 percent convenience fee on cards. Drop boxes are on site.
  • Bank bill pay: your parcel ID is the account number, and tax counts as paid on the day the county receives it, not the day your bank sends it.

The county also runs a free ACH withdrawal program. For 2026 the sign-up cutoff for the May payment was April 10 and for the October payment was September 11. Withdrawals happen on May 10 and October 10 for homes. A transfer of the property can end the enrollment, and the county decides by the recording date of the deed, so tell the office in writing if you sell shortly before a withdrawal.

sections.h2: What is Rochester like for someone selling a house there?
sections.html:
Rochester is a southeast Minnesota city on the South Fork of the Zumbro River, about 85 miles from the Twin Cities, and its housing market follows the medical economy that grew around Mayo Clinic. George Head founded the town in 1854, and the city was incorporated in 1858. After the 1883 tornado, William Mayo and his sons cared for the injured, which led to St. Marys Hospital opening in 1889.

Mayo Clinic is the core employer, and the 2013 Destination Medical Center law set up a state-backed plan for downtown districts around the clinic and the river. IBM's campus and Rochester Public Schools are also among the larger employers listed for the city. A major flood in 1978 pushed the city into a large flood-control project along the Zumbro and nearby streams, which matters when a buyer asks about low-lying lots.

Weather shapes the condition of a Rochester house. The city averages about 51.9 inches of snow and 33 inches of rain a year, is among the windiest in the country, and was hit by tornadoes in 2010 on the northwest side near Lincolnshire and in 2019 in southwest Rochester. The Census Bureau gives these figures for the city:

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $310,500, against $332,700 nationally.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 65.1 percent, across 51,131 households of about 2.34 people.
  • Median gross rent: $1,399. Median owner cost with a mortgage: $1,864 a month.
  • Residents who lived in the same house a year earlier: 83.0 percent, a lower share than the 87.7 percent for the country.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Rochester property valuation?
sections.html:
Start with the Olmsted County Assessor at 507-328-7670, with a recent appraisal or recent sales of similar homes in hand.

If that does not settle it, go to the appeal meeting printed on your valuation notice. A city or township that has its own local board is where you begin, and one without a board goes straight to the county board. Under Minnesota Statutes section 274.01, local boards meet between April 1 and May 31, and they may not cut the assessor's total by more than 1 percent. The county board meets in mid-June.

The last step is a petition to the Minnesota Tax Court, filed after your notice arrives and before April 30 of the year the tax is payable. Since 2023 the petition must also be served on the county auditor. Olmsted County accepts service by email at olmcotaxpetitionservice@olmstedcounty.gov or by hand delivery to the County Attorney's Office, 151 Fourth Street Southeast. The Tax Court's phone number is 651-539-3260.

sections.h2: Which relief programs can lower a Rochester owner's tax?
sections.html:
The main ones run through the state, and the county lists them for Rochester owners. Homestead applications are due December 15 and exempt property applications February 1. Green Acres applications for farmland are due May 1.

  • Regular property tax refund, often called the circuit breaker, based on household income and the tax you pay.
  • Special refund, available when net tax rises by at least 12 percent and $100, with no income test. Both refunds use Form M1PR.
  • Senior citizen property tax deferral, applied for through the Minnesota Department of Revenue on Form CR-SCD.
  • Credit of $120 per month served for members of the military in a combat zone or hazardous duty area.

Truth in Taxation notices go out in mid-November. They estimate next year's tax if each taxing body adopts the budget it is considering, and they list meeting dates. The notice leaves out special assessments and referendums that voters approve in November, so the final figure can run higher.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax when I sell a Rochester house?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax follows the parcel, so the closing agent needs the current payoff from the county before a deed is recorded. For a past-due year, call 507-328-7635 for the exact amount. Taxes that stay unpaid long enough can end in forfeiture, where title to the land and buildings vests in the State of Minnesota.

A sale also changes who receives paperwork. The county mails one statement each year in late March to the address you gave at closing, and it does not mail statements for mid-year purchases. Tax details can also appear in your closing documents. When the deed is recorded, a certificate of value is filed with the county auditor under section 272.115, and the assessor drops the homestead classification for the next assessment year unless the buyer applies and qualifies.

If you own a Rochester house with tax behind and want a quick sale, gather the parcel ID, your latest statement and the payoff figure first. If automatic withdrawal is on, send the county a written stop request, since a recorded transfer may end it only after the recording date.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Rochester, MN?
faqs.a: Olmsted County Property Records and Licensing collects it, at 151 4th Street SE in Rochester, and the Olmsted County Assessor sets the value. Call 507-328-7636 for statement questions.

faqs.q: Is the second half of 2026 Rochester property tax still payable?
faqs.a: Yes, but it is late. The second half of real property tax was due October 15, 2026, and Minnesota adds a 2 percent homestead or 4 percent nonhomestead penalty on the due date, with more added each month. Agricultural and manufactured home second halves are due November 16, 2026.

faqs.q: Can I pay Rochester property tax by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. Online and phone card payments carry a 3.28 percent fee, and an e-check costs $3.16. At the Government Center counter a card carries a 2.15 percent fee, while cash and checks have none.

faqs.q: How do I get a copy of my Rochester tax statement?
faqs.a: Print it from the Olmsted County property information website, or call 507-328-7636. A reprint at the office costs $2, so keep the original mailed in March.

faqs.q: Does automatic withdrawal stop when I sell my Rochester home?
faqs.a: Not always right away. The county says a transfer of the property may end the enrollment, but the timing follows the recording date of the deed and is not guaranteed. Tell the county in writing if a withdrawal date is near.
